# Goal: two adversarial passes, both outside the review loops

Every `file:line` below points into the tree this was written against — `94c402a`, before either pass existed. The change moved those lines; the file names and the identifiers named beside them are what to search on.

Add a **premise challenge** to the plan forge and a **final challenge** to the ship pipeline. Both are single bounded passes that run where no loop runs, and neither is a reviewer dimension.

## Why these two positions and no others

Tagteam already applies adversarial pressure everywhere a loop runs, and none at the two edges: the moment before a loop starts, and the moment one ends.

Inside the loops it is covered. `reviewAssignments` (`workflows/ship-pr.js:881`) routes every dimension to the engine that did not write the last fix, and `independentCoverage` (`workflows/ship-pr.js:1561`) refuses `clean` until that independent engine has a result for every selected dimension, so no fix is ever cleared by its own author. The loop breaks at `maxReviewLoops` before the fix phase (`workflows/ship-pr.js:1578`), so no fix ever ships unreviewed. The specialist pre-pass (`workflows/ship-pr.js:1277`) puts six lenses in front of round one and makes every round-one reviewer adopt or reject each item. `prompts/claim-verification.md` is the adversarial discipline itself.

The two gaps are at the edges.

**A premise is asserted and never attacked.** `workflows/plan-forge.js:2056-2105` obtains the premises from one call on one engine. That model labels each row `verified` or `assumed` itself, and `prompts/plan-premises-codex.md` asks only that `basis` *name* a file, symbol, migration, or command — nothing checks that the named file says what the basis claims. `commands/plan.md:60` asks the `assumed` rows and reaches `verified` ones only if fewer than four assumed ones exist. So a confidently wrong `verified` premise passes the one gate built to catch this class of defect, and `skills/tagteam/SKILL.md:89` states what that costs: no reviewer can find it, because every reviewer reads the same document and inherits it.

**Nothing looks at a candidate once it goes clean.** When the loop breaks at `workflows/ship-pr.js:1569`, the next thing that happens is gate assembly at `workflows/ship-pr.js:1756` and then a human. Every reviewer that produced that clean state was scoped to a dimension charter; nobody argues about the change as a whole — whether it does what the PR contract says, whether its tests assert behavior or shape, whether the accumulated fixes drifted it away from its task. This is structurally the same argument that removed post-clean compaction from the plan forge (`skills/tagteam/SKILL.md:95`): the step no check covers, at the moment the artifact is otherwise finished. Here it is not an edit that goes unchecked but a state.

## What this deliberately does not do

Neither pass is added as a reviewer dimension, and `config.reviewers` is not touched, so dimension selection, per-dimension gates, and tier routing are unchanged.

An adversarial reviewer inside the plan cross-review loop is ruled out by the divergence detector's own rationale (`skills/tagteam/SKILL.md:97`): contradiction surface grows with the document, so such a reviewer always finds something, the blocking-plus-major count stops strictly falling, and passes that were converging stop with `divergence`. It would defeat the stop condition it runs under.

An adversarial dimension inside the ship review loop is ruled out by cost and by severity: it multiplies by rounds and engines against `limits.agentCallsPerPr`, and severity is what feeds the fixer, so speculative findings would go straight into a `workspace-write` repair.

Pre-fix refutation of findings is not included. The last configured round never fixes, and `independentCoverage` already forces a non-author engine to clear every fix, so a false positive costs churn rather than silent breakage. Add it only if ship ledgers show real false-positive churn; `occurrences` and `status: fix-failed` in the saved ledger already measure it.

## Phase 1 — the premise challenge

**Where.** Inside the existing gate block at `workflows/plan-forge.js:2056`, after `stated` is obtained and before the `needs-premises-confirmation` return at `workflows/plan-forge.js:2104`. It inherits that gate's entry conditions unchanged: a resume, a continuation, and any invocation already carrying `premisesFile` skip it, so it costs per plan, not per pass.

**Engine.** The engine that did not state them. `useClaude` (`workflows/plan-forge.js:1637`) decides the stating engine, so under `--provider both` Claude states and Codex challenges. Under `--provider claude` or `--provider codex` there is no other engine, and the challenge still runs: every dispatch in this plugin is a fresh agent or a fresh `codex exec` process with no memory of the call that stated the premises, so a same-engine challenger is still an independent reader of the repository. The record says which it was through `independent: false`.

**How the premises reach the challenger.** By whichever route is already free, and a new file only where none is.

- `--provider claude`: the challenger is a Claude agent in the same workflow, so the premises travel inline through `fenced()` (`workflows/plan-forge.js:727`) in the prompt body. There is no per-argument ceiling on a prompt body — the 11,336-character incident at `workflows/plan-forge.js:3176` was an inline *command argument*, stopped by `assembleCommand` (`:850-856`) — so this costs nothing.
- `--provider codex`: the stated premises are already on disk as the bridge's own artifact (`reviews/<passId>-premises-codex.json`, `workflows/plan-forge.js:2083`). The challenger fences that path.
- `--provider both` only: Claude stated them and Codex must read them, so they are persisted once to `reviews/<passId>-premises-stated.json` at mode 0600 through a `tagteam:scribe` dispatch verified with `scripts/verify-payload.mjs`, the way the specialist list is at `workflows/ship-pr.js:1341`. This is the one case with no free route. The expected checksum must describe the object that lands on disk — `verify-payload.mjs` tokenizes the whole parsed file — and not the array inside it, which is how the specialist precedent computes it because that call persists a bare array; the same token is bound again at compose time so the bytes are checked once more before they reach Codex. Plan-forge has never dispatched the scribe, so `planAgent` (`workflows/plan-forge.js:967`) must count `tagteam:scribe` in its plumbing branch at `:969`, or the persist is reported as substantive Claude reasoning in `usage` and missing from `plumbingCallsByModel`.

**Contract.** For each premise, in order, visit the cited basis and try to falsify the claim. One row per premise, `verdict` one of:

- `contradicted` — the repository shows something incompatible with the claim. Requires counter-evidence naming a file and the smallest useful line range and stating what the repository actually shows.
- `unsupported` — the cited basis does not establish the claim, though nothing contradicts it. Requires quoting what the basis does say.
- `unchallenged` — the basis was checked and holds up.

**Only `contradicted` puts a premise in doubt.** A `contradicted` verdict downgrades a `verified` premise to `assumed`. An `unsupported` verdict downgrades nothing: it is shown to the person and ranked ahead of the unchallenged rows, and the premise keeps its status. "The file you cited does not really say this" is satisfiable against almost any 400-character basis and needs no counter-fact, so letting it downgrade would flag most rows and turn a four-question gate into a long one — the same always-finds-something failure this document refuses for the loop reviewers. A contradiction has to produce a conflicting fact, which is what makes it worth a person's attention.

**Alignment is checked, not requested.** The returned list must have exactly one row per stated premise, and `challenges[i].claim` must match `stated.premises[i].claim` under a normalization that folds whitespace, case, dashes, and quotes. The comparison folds formatting — whitespace, case, dashes, quotes — and nothing more: a claim that came back saying something else is drift and still discards the challenge. Byte equality is the direction this repository already had to retreat from once, when grading a model on retyping carried text verbatim read a compliant restatement as a silent drop. On any mismatch the whole challenge is discarded and logged rather than applied: a misaligned row downgrades the wrong premise, and prose telling a model not to reorder is not a check.

**Invariant: no model path raises a premise's confidence.** The challenge can downgrade `verified` to `assumed` and can annotate; nothing in the workflow moves a premise the other way. A person still can — that is the entire point of the gate — but a challenged row may not be settled by the bulk "All of these hold" option: it is asked on its own, showing the counter-evidence, and needs its own answer. `commands/plan.md:62` sets `kind: "verified"` for anything the human confirms or corrects, which is correct for a human answer and would otherwise silently re-promote a downgraded row through a bulk confirm.

**Counter-evidence is the challenger's claim, not repository fact.** It is model prose, and a hallucinated contradiction that pushes a person to "correct" a true premise is worse than no challenge at all, because `workflows/plan-forge.js:1922` then tells the drafter the premises are settled and must not be re-derived. So it is presented as what the challenger says it found, with its `file:line` shown so the person can look, and never as an established fact.

**Schema.** New `schemas/plan-premise-challenge.schema.json`: `{challenges: [{claim, verdict, evidence?, basisChecked}]}`, `additionalProperties: false`, `maxItems: 20` matching the premises schema.

**Return shape.** `needs-premises-confirmation` gains `premiseChallenge: {engine, independent, ran, challenges: [...]}` and `premises` carries the downgrades already applied. The premise rows keep exactly `{claim, basis, kind}`: `schemas/plan-premises.schema.json` is `additionalProperties: false` and `commands/plan.md:62` writes the settled file in that same shape back to `CONFIRMED_PREMISES` (`workflows/plan-forge.js:2318`), so counter-evidence lives in the `premiseChallenge` block, keyed by index, and never on a premise row.

**A lost challenge never costs the premises.** The Codex path must catch the failure itself: `optional: true` marks the dispatch record (`workflows/plan-forge.js:1434`) and does not suppress the throw in `relayCodex`, and the only other optional caller survives it because it sits inside `parallel()`, which turns a throw into null. So the call is wrapped, the fatal checkpoint it raised is dropped with it, and `premiseChallenge: {ran: false, reason}` is returned with the stated premises intact. The dispatch stays in the unconfirmed receipts, because Codex may still have been paid. Without that, a relay loss after the premise call has been paid for would throw, and `commands/plan.md:78` only skips this gate once a `drafts/*-premises.json` exists — which it does not yet — so a `kind: "fresh"` resume would pay for the premises a second time.

**Cost.** Under `--provider claude`, two Claude calls where there was one. Under `--provider codex`, `codexReasoning` is two dispatches per pass (`buildPrompt` at `:1732`, `relayCodex` at `:1765`), so four where there were two. Under `--provider both`, one Claude call, one scribe persist, and one Codex challenge of two dispatches. Once per plan, never per pass.

**The verdict travels on the row.** A challenged premise carries `challenged: "contradicted" | "unsupported"`, so the command filters structurally instead of correlating two lists by position in prose — the correlation this same block refuses to trust. The marker never reaches the settled file, which keeps the `{claim, basis, kind}` shape `schemas/plan-premises.schema.json` pins.

## Phase 2 — the final challenge

**Where.** In `workflows/ship-pr.js`, after the review loop, only when `status === "clean"`, before the `gateFailures` assembly at `workflows/ship-pr.js:1756`. It runs against `candidateOid` and the `snapshotValue` the clean round already computed for that exact commit, so it needs no new snapshot.

**Engine.** The engine that did not perform the last fix. When the loop went clean with no fix at all, the opposite of `config.review.firstReviewer`, normalized through `selectedEngine` (`workflows/ship-pr.js:303`) so a single-provider run stays on its provider.

**Contract.** A dimension-free charter at `prompts/final-challenge.md`, with `prompts/final-challenge-codex.md` for the bridge: this change is about to be proposed for merge and every dimension reviewer has cleared it; argue that it must not merge. What to attack is the whole-change level no charter covers — the diff against its PR contract, behavior claimed versus behavior implemented, tests that assert shape rather than outcome, and any earlier round's fix that changed what the task meant. Findings are `blocking` or `major` only, each with a concrete failure path (inputs or state, then the wrong outcome) bound to a file and the smallest useful line range. There is no cap on how many it may return. An empty result is the expected result and the charter says so, because a pass that returns something every time converts every clean ship into a human gate.

**Invariant: this workflow never auto-fixes a challenge finding.** Findings are pushed onto the ledger explicitly — `mergeLedger` (`workflows/ship-pr.js:417`) hard-codes `status: "open"`, so it cannot express this — with `id: stableId(finding)`, `dimension: "final-challenge"`, and `status: "needs-human"`. `stableId` matters because `scripts/render-report.mjs` prints the ID in its human-decision list. `actionable()` (`:433`) counts `needs-human` at blocking or major, and `fixTargets` (`:1572`) excludes it, so the finding gates without ever reaching a fixer. A human may still ask for a repair afterwards through the `repairFindings` path in `commands/ship.md:79`; that is a person's decision and creates a new candidate, which re-arms every gate as it should.

**Every result answers for it.** `finish` defaults `finalChallenge` to `{ran: false, reason: "not-reached"}`, so a run that stopped before the loop still says so, and the record is threaded through the relay and capacity returns rather than dropped there; `capacityGate` concatenates gate failures instead of replacing them, so a finding raised just before the limit is not discarded by it. The reasons are distinct facts — `not-reached`, `not-clean`, `disabled`, `unknown-tier`, `agent-call-budget`, `no-result` — because a repository that switched the gate off is not a candidate that never went clean. A configuration written before this key existed never named a tier and need not define one called `standard`; an unknown tier reports a gate that did not run rather than throwing away the invocation on its last call.

**Gate and acceptance.** A surviving finding is pushed onto `gateFailures`, which the expression at `workflows/ship-pr.js:1768` already turns into `failed-gates`. `final-challenge` is not a key in `config.reviewers`, so the per-dimension loop at `:1759` ignores it and the push is explicit. From there the existing gate flow in `commands/ship.md` applies with no new surface: the run stops for a human, who may `Merge it` — which records approval **against the current candidate only** — or send it back, or stop. That is the accept-and-continue path, and it already has the right lifetime: `bindNewCandidate` (`scripts/lib/gates.mjs:20`) wipes every gate when a new candidate appears, and `gateIsCurrent` (`:59`) checks the candidate OID **and** the policy fingerprint. An acceptance therefore dies with the bytes it was read against, and a CI repair or later fix re-runs the challenge on the new candidate. Human approval already satisfies ordinary review gates, so an accepted finding does not by itself force a manual merge. Nothing loops: the challenge cannot write code, so it can never create the new candidate that would re-arm it.

**A challenge that did not run is not a pass.** No call is reserved inside the round loop: `estimatedCalls` (`workflows/ship-pr.js:1387`) is computed per round and its shortfall path returns `agent-budget-gate` before the round runs, so a reservation there would both charge every round and make the not-run record unreachable. The budget is checked after the clean break, immediately before dispatch. If it cannot be covered, the result records `finalChallenge: {ran: false, reason}` and pushes a gate failure naming that the last gate did not run. This borrows the *classification* `README.md:107` applies to CI — skipped is recorded as not run, never as passed — while blocking rather than proceeding, because unlike CI this gate has no independent evidence behind it: the whole point is that a clean candidate has nothing else left to check it.

**Cost.** Two to four calls per PR: the challenge itself (a Codex challenger goes through `codexCall`, whose relay is its own dispatch plus up to `RELAY_ATTEMPTS` re-reads) and one scribe dispatch to persist the record, because a workflow script cannot write files (`skills/tagteam/SKILL.md:290`). Clean ships only. A ship that already failed its gates does not buy a second opinion it cannot act on.

**Record.** `scripts/append-review-event.mjs` currently throws on any event kind but `fix` (`:18`) and requires `event.round === highestRound` (`:35`), so it gains a `final-challenge` render and the event carries the clean round number. The rendered block must not collide with the artifact grammar in `scripts/parse-review-artifact.mjs`: its heading is not `## Round` or `### Reviewer`, and its bullets do not begin `- F<round>.<n> |` or `- S<n> |`, so the appender's own before/after parse still passes. The machine-readable copy is `prs/<pr-id>/final-challenge.json`, written by the same scribe call. It is a record, not a gate cache: nothing reuses it, because the ledger is rebuilt fresh on every invocation (`workflows/ship-pr.js:1265`) and a gate that outlived its candidate is the failure the gate machinery exists to prevent.

**Dry runs need no decision.** `commands/ship.md:33` creates no worktree, no branch, and invokes no model under `--dry-run`, so `ship-pr` never runs and there is nothing to skip.

## Configuration

Two keys, one version move.

- `planning.premiseChallenge`: boolean, default true. Goes in the `planning` object, which is `additionalProperties: false` (`schemas/config.schema.json:18`).
- `review.finalChallenge`: `{enabled: boolean, tier: "deep"|"standard"|"light"}`, default enabled at **standard**. The challenge runs on every clean ship — the path that is going well — so `deep` (`opus/xhigh` plus `gpt-5.6-sol/high`) would make the most expensive call in the pipeline unconditional against a 60-call budget. The `review` object is `additionalProperties: false` with only `firstReviewer` today (`schemas/config.schema.json:161`).

Configuration goes to version 4: `CONFIG_VERSION` (`scripts/validate-json.mjs:102`), `VERSION_KEYS[4]` (`:107`), the `version` enum (`schemas/config.schema.json:12`), and the literal `3` in `commands/init.md:97` (upgrade step 5) and `:111` (write step 2). Three further pinned copies must move with them: `examples/config.json:2`, which `test/config-upgrade.test.mjs:67` asserts equals `CONFIG_VERSION`; the sentence at `skills/tagteam/SKILL.md:59` naming which version the plugin writes; and **this repository's own `.tagteam/config.json`**, which is version 3 — leaving it stale would make `/tagteam:plan` on tagteam itself hard-stop for an upgrade, breaking self-hosting on the commit that adds the feature.

`--upgrade` derives the key *list* from the validator's output, but `commands/init.md` §Upgrade step 3 requires the question *wording* to exist in that document, so both keys need Interview question blocks. Once `CONFIG_VERSION` is 4, `scripts/validate-json.mjs:247-251` makes both keys hard-required at that version, so a configuration upgraded after the first pull request carries a `review.finalChallenge` that nothing reads until the second lands. That window is accepted because no release ships between them.

The plugin patch version moves 0.5.11 to 0.5.12 across `package.json`, `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, and `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, which `test/version-consistency.test.mjs` requires to stay identical.

## Tests

- Premise challenge: `contradicted` downgrades a `verified` premise; `unsupported` never downgrades anything; a challenge whose row count or claims do not line up with the stated premises is discarded whole; the challenger runs on the opposite engine under `both` and records `independent: false` under a single provider; the persist happens only under `both` and a failed `verify-payload` does not silently substitute inlined text; a lost Codex challenge returns `ran: false` with the premises intact; a resume or continuation carrying `premisesFile` never dispatches one.
- Final challenge: it runs only on `status === "clean"`; findings land as `needs-human` with a `stableId` and are excluded from `fixTargets`; a surviving finding turns `clean` into `failed-gates`; a budget too small produces a gate failure rather than a silent skip; no additional call is reserved inside the round loop.
- `scripts/append-review-event.mjs`: a `final-challenge` event renders, appends, and leaves `parseReviewArtifact` reporting `ok`; an unknown kind still throws.
- Provider routing: cases in `test/plan-provider-routing.test.mjs` and `test/ship-provider-routing.test.mjs` for both passes under `both`, `claude`, and `codex`.
- Configuration: `test/config-upgrade.test.mjs` gains the version-4 case, and its version-1 and version-2 `deepEqual` expectations at `:41` and `:61` go stale and must be updated.
- Prompts: `test/prompt-integrity.test.mjs` cases for the two new Codex templates.
- Agents: `agents/premise-challenger.md` and `agents/final-challenger.md`, read-only, with no `Bash` in `tools:`, which `test/agent-authorization.test.mjs` already checks. Both must also be added to the `allowed-tools` `Agent(...)` list in `commands/plan.md:4` and `commands/ship.md:4`, along with `tagteam:scribe` for plan-forge's persist.

## Acceptance criteria

- A fresh `/tagteam:plan` against a repository where a stated `verified` premise is contradicted by the code puts that premise to the person with the challenger's counter-evidence attached, before any plan text exists.
- No workflow path raises a premise's confidence, and a downgraded row cannot be settled by a bulk confirmation.
- A ship whose review loop goes clean either records a final challenge bound to that exact candidate OID, or fails its gates naming that the challenge did not run.
- Agent counts per review round are unchanged: nothing is reserved or spent inside the loop.
- `.tagteam/config.json`, `examples/config.json`, and the schema all read version 4, and `/tagteam:plan` still runs against this repository itself.
- `npm test` and `npm run check` pass.

## PR sequence

1. **Premise challenge, and the configuration version move.** Workflow gate, schema, prompt template, agent, command section, both configuration keys, example and self-config, init wording, SKILL.md, version bump, tests.
2. **Final challenge.** Workflow pass, prompt template, agent, ledger and gate wiring, `append-review-event.mjs`, ship command rendering, tests.

The second depends on the first only for the configuration key it reads. Nothing else is shared, and nothing is released between them.

## Open questions

None. The four that stood open — single-provider behavior, dry runs, what a human may do with a surviving finding, and a cap on findings — are settled above.
